title: Population Models with Harvesting
short: Add harvesting to logistic growth and find the new equilibria.

blocks.html: A fishery, a forest or a deer herd grows roughly logistically, $P' = rP\left(1 - \frac{P}{K}\right)$. Harvesting removes some of the population. The phase line shows at once whether a harvest is sustainable, and what happens when it is not.

With a constant harvest $H$: $$P' = rP\left(1 - \frac{P}{K}\right) - H.$$ If $0 < H < \frac{rK}{4}$ there are two equilibria: the lower one is an unstable threshold and the upper one is stable. At $H = \frac{rK}{4}$ (the maximum sustainable yield) they merge; for larger $H$ there is no equilibrium and the population collapses.

The natural growth $g(P) = rP\left(1 - \frac{P}{K}\right)$ is a downward parabola with roots 0 and $K$ and its peak at $P = \frac{K}{2}$, where $g = \frac{rK}{4}$. The population grows exactly where the parabola lies above the horizontal line at height $H$. The crossings are the equilibria. As $H$ rises, the line climbs, the crossings move together, touch at the peak, and then disappear. A sudden change like this, as a parameter passes a critical value, is called a bifurcation.

blocks.title: Two equilibria
blocks.q: A fish population (in thousands) follows $P' = 0.5P\left(1 - \frac{P}{100}\right) - 8$. Find and classify the equilibria.
steps: $P'$ $= -0.005(P - 20)(P - 80)$: negative below 20, positive between, negative above 80.
blocks.a: $P = 20$ is unstable (a collapse threshold); $P = 80$ is stable.

blocks.title: The largest sustainable harvest
blocks.q: For the same fishery, what is the largest constant harvest with an equilibrium?
blocks.a: $H = 12.5$ thousand fish per year, with the population held at 50.

blocks.title: Constant effort instead
blocks.q: Suppose fishing removes a fixed fraction, $P' = 0.5P\left(1 - \frac{P}{100}\right) - 0.2P$. Find the positive equilibrium and the yield there.
blocks.a: $P = 60$ (stable), yield 12. Constant effort never removes the equilibrium entirely, which is one reason it is safer.

blocks.name: de-phaseline

opts.task: Raise the harvest $H$ past 12.5 and watch the two equilibria merge and vanish.

blocks.cap: Left: $f(P) = 0.5P(1 - P/100) - H$ on its side, with the phase line. Right: population curves. Below the unstable threshold every curve falls; once $H > 12.5$ every curve falls.

blocks.html: Treating the maximum sustainable yield as a safe target. At $H = \frac{rK}{4}$ the single equilibrium is semi-stable: any dip below $\frac{K}{2}$, from a bad year or a counting error, starts a slide to collapse. Another slip is calling the lower equilibrium stable because it is “the smaller population”; check the arrows on both sides.
